Package simple.file

Class CSVRow

java.lang.Object
simple.file.CSVRow
public final class CSVRow extends Object
Utility class to handle a single CSV row.

This class represents a row from a CSV file. It allows retrieving column values using column names and parsing them into specific types.

It stores the values of the row as a list and the headers of the CSV as a map to associate each column name with its index.

  • Constructor Details

    • CSVRow

      public CSVRow(List<String> values, Map<String,Integer> headerMap)
      Creates a CSVRow instance.

      This constructor initializes a CSV row with the provided values and header map. The values list contains the actual data for the row, while the headerMap associates each column name with its index in the row.

      Parameters:
      values - A list of string values representing a row in the CSV.
      headerMap - A map that associates column names with their index positions in the row.

  • Method Details

    • get

      public final <T> T get(String columnName, Class<T> type)
      Retrieves the value from the CSV row for a specific column, converting it to the specified type.

      The method uses the column name to find the corresponding index in the headerMap, retrieves the value from the values list, and then attempts to convert it to the specified type.

      Type Parameters:
      T - The type of the value to return.
      Parameters:
      columnName - The name of the column to retrieve the value from.
      type - The type to which the value should be converted (e.g., Integer.class, String.class).
      Returns:
      The value from the CSV row cast to the specified type, or null if the value is empty or not found.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - If the type provided is unsupported.

    • getValues

      public final List<String> getValues()
      Returns the list of all values in the row.

      This method returns the values of the CSV row as a list of strings, where each element in the list corresponds to a value in the row, based on the order of the columns.

      Returns:
      A list of strings containing the values of the CSV row.
